concept_prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: final in-game environment concept for a redesigned TOOL STORAGE ROOM in a Chinese industrial prison escape game.
Input 1 role: current editor screenshot, authoritative room footprint, axis alignment, door locations and visual style reference. Red box selects a narrow vertical tool room; ignore all editor UI/selection marks.
Input 2 role: original campus masterplan reference, desired dense perimeter tool cabinets and stored equipment, compact readable room identity.
Primary request: redesign only the tool room into a polished buildable game environment closely matching the original masterplan. Show one large complete roof-removed room concept, NOT a sheet of unrelated objects or a presentation with text panels.
Camera: same high overhead orthographic 2.5D painted game view as reference, vertical room walls vertical and horizontal walls horizontal, no diagonal isometric or perspective convergence. Interior footprint about 360 wide x 540 deep, portrait rectangular. Furniture appropriate for an 80-unit-tall game character, cabinet depth only 45-65 world units, main walkable aisle at least 120 units wide. Include a narrow view of the paved passage outside bottom and left, a slight hint of workshop on far left and warehouse exterior on far right. Landscape or near-square canvas with the tool room taking most of the image. No game/editor UI, no red boxes, no route arrows.
Architecture and access invariants: retain both existing doors, one on the LEFT wall around the middle-lower section, the other centered in the BOTTOM wall. Do not add a top or right doorway. Both door openings shown clearly with threshold and appropriate partly open blue-grey utility steel door leaves without blocking the middle aisle. Keep both routes connected. The room has walls, cream coping, worn warm pale plaster uppers and desaturated blue-grey painted lower wall panels, narrow metal trim. Give it a distinct utilitarian tool-custody identity instead of copying clinic green ceramic tiles. The floor consists of compact dark warm-grey industrial concrete tiles with restrained wear, thin yellow worn cabinet-front markers; no grass inside, no heavy full-room hazard striping.
Furnishing layout: along TOP wall, a wide low steel drawer bench with modest dark wood worktop and mounted perforated tool pegboard, a small orderly selection of wrench, pliers, screwdriver, hacksaw silhouettes and missing-tool hooks. This is an issue/checking bench not a heavy machine workbench. Upper LEFT side has one full-height narrow worn blue-grey lockable tool cabinet and a small shallow shelf of labeled cases. RIGHT side has two shallow sturdy open steel parts racks holding small brown boxes, hand-tool cases and olive toolboxes, with a small drawer cabinet between; do not fill with warehouse pallets. Lower LEFT corner below the side entrance has a short return/checking cabinet with shallow tool trays and a small clipboard, keeping bottom door access clear. Lower RIGHT corner has a compact stand of neatly coiled cable and a small locked specialist-tool chest, all tucked against walls. Central strip deliberately clear with enough space to walk and stand in front of shelves. Dense but organized perimeter, no scattered garbage or obstacles on walking floor.
Accents: small ivory plaque reading exactly "工具房", a clipped sheet reading "领用登记" near the top checking bench, a few cabinet number plates, old wall clock and one caged wall lamp. Tiny industrial yellow details, restrained rust and paint chipping, no excessive gritty texture. No cashier, no medical apparatus, no beds, no toilets, no grand machinery, no people.
Style: sharp hand-painted 2D game assets, warm-grey walls and cold blue-grey steel balanced by dark honey-brown wood and kraft cartons, clean crisp dark edge outlines, visible bolts and handles at usable sprite scale, top-left soft daylight, subtle cast shadows, consistent scale and credible small room. Precise silhouettes, no blurry or sandy noisy finish. Match artistic quality and perspective of the supplied game's reference. No title banner, no infographic labels, no giant floating room name.
door_refinement_prompt: Edit this tool-room final concept with ONE tightly controlled correction. Keep the same image composition, camera, every shelf, cabinet, pegboard, workbench, tool, texture, lighting, wall colors and left-side door. Correct ONLY the bottom-center entry: the approved game footprint has a 180-unit doorway in a 360-unit-wide interior, so widen the bottom opening to approximately HALF the room interior width, keeping it centered. Render a coherent pair of two partially open matching blue-grey utility steel door leaves, one attached to each jamb, with worn yellow small hardware accents; no missing top halves, no walls crossing the leaf faces. The bottom threshold is continuous with the corridor and main aisle and visibly passable. Shorten the two bottom facade wall sections accordingly and keep their end/jamb details clean. Keep bottom-left return cabinet and bottom-right cable stand/chest where they are unless a tiny clearance adjustment is essential. Do not change the top wall, tool-room label, left door, surrounding workshop/warehouse, shape of room, or any other part. No new text, no UI, no annotation.
